Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments

accepted.s: The first pilot use of an Electronic Voting Machine in India was conducted in which constituency and year?
o: Anantnag Assembly constituency, Jammu and Kashmir, in 1998
accepted.x: EVMs were first used on a pilot basis in the 70-Parur Assembly constituency of Kerala in 1982.
accepted.tq: Use the exact place-year combination rather than confusing a pilot with a wider trial or statewide use.
accepted.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The wider trial of Electronic Voting Machines in 1998 covered how many Assembly seats in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Delhi?
accepted.x: The wider trial in 1998 covered 16 Assembly seats across Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Delhi.
accepted.tq: Fix the specific numerical milestone in the EVM timeline.
accepted.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Electronic Voting Machines were used at all polling stations in a Lok Sabha general election for the first time in:
accepted.x: The 2004 general election was the first Lok Sabha election in which EVMs were used at all polling stations.
accepted.tq: Distinguish nationwide polling-station coverage from the first state-level use.
accepted.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the manufacture and legal framework of EVMs and VVPATs is correct?
o: They are manufactured only by the Election Commission of India under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
They are manufactured by BEL and ECIL, and the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 were amended to permit VVPATs.
They are manufactured by the Reserve Bank of India, and the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 prohibit VVPAT use.
They are manufactured by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, and VVPATs were authorised by the Constitution.
accepted.x: Bharat Electronics Limited and Electronics Corporation of India Limited manufacture the machines. The Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 were amended to enable VVPAT use.
accepted.tq: Check both the manufacturing bodies and the specific legal instrument instead of accepting a constitutional or ministry attribution.
accepted.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In N. Chandrababu Naidu v. Union of India (2019), VVPAT slips of how many randomly selected EVMs per Assembly segment were directed to be counted?
accepted.x: The Supreme Court directed counting of VVPAT slips from five randomly selected EVMs in each Assembly segment.
accepted.tq: Identify the court case through its distinctive verification number.
accepted.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Supreme Court's 2024 decision in ADR v. ECI:
1. The demand for ballot paper voting and counting of 100 per cent VVPAT slips was rejected.
2. Symbol-loading units are to be sealed and preserved for 45 days.
3. A runner-up in second or third position may seek checking of 5 per cent of EVMs per segment within seven days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the verification rules associated with ADR v. ECI in April 2024.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of linked judicial safeguards using the coded combination options.
accepted.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

accepted.s: VVPAT slips must be counted in which of the following circumstances?
o: Whenever EVM data and Form 17C do not match
Whenever postal ballots exceed the number of EVM votes
Only in constituencies using postal ballots
Only when the winning candidate requests it after the declaration of results
accepted.x: VVPAT slips are required to be counted wherever the EVM data and Form 17C do not match.
accepted.tq: Apply the verification rule to a specific discrepancy rather than to a general recount demand.
accepted.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following features was specified for EVMs in relation to candidate identification?
o: They must display the candidates' party manifestos.
They must show black-and-white photographs of polling agents.
They must show colour photographs of the candidates.
They must display only the candidates' election symbols without names.
accepted.x: EVMs are to display colour photographs of the candidates.
accepted.tq: Use the precise official feature and reject nearby but unsupported display requirements.
accepted.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is the correct order of counting-related procedures?
A. Counting of postal ballots
B. Counting of the penultimate EVM/VVPAT round
C. Counting of the final EVM/VVPAT round
accepted.x: Postal ballots are counted before the penultimate EVM/VVPAT round; the final EVM/VVPAT round follows subsequently.
accepted.tq: Arrange the procedure by identifying the expressly stated precedence of postal-ballot counting.
accepted.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to totalisers, consider the following statements:
1. A totaliser combines the counting of several EVMs.
2. It is intended to conceal booth-wise voting trends.
3. The Election Commission has stated that a legal framework for totalisers already exists.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: A totaliser combines several EVM counts to hide booth-wise trends. The ECI stated that no legal framework for totalisers exists, making statement 3 false.
accepted.tq: Spot the reversed institutional position in the third statement.
accepted.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs relating to Delimitation Commissions is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The 1973 Commission was chaired by Justice J.L. Kapur. Justice Kuldip Singh chaired the 2002 Commission.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped chairperson in a date-person matching question.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the years of the Delimitation Acts from the years in which the corresponding Commissions were constituted?
accepted.x: The Delimitation Acts were enacted in 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002, while the Commissions were constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely related years of legislation from the years of constitution of the Commissions.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Read the following statements:
1. Article 82 deals with readjustment of Lok Sabha constituencies after each census.
2. Article 170 deals with readjustment of State Legislative Assembly constituencies after each census.
3. Articles 330 and 332 relate to reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Articles 82 and 170 provide for readjustment relating to Parliament and State Assemblies, while Articles 330 and 332 concern SC/ST seat reservation.
accepted.tq: Match constitutional Articles with their institutional subject before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Delimitation primarily refers to:
o: Fixing the number of seats and the boundaries of Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies
Allocating ministerial portfolios among political parties
Determining the expenditure limit of each political party
Preparing the electoral roll for municipal elections only
accepted.x: Delimitation is the fixing of the number of seats and boundaries of Lok Sabha and State Assembly constituencies.
accepted.tq: Choose the definition that covers both the numerical and territorial aspects of delimitation.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The constitutional principle underlying delimitation is best expressed as:
o: One State, one vote, one value
One district, one representative, one value
One party, one constituency, one value
One person, one vote, one value
accepted.x: Delimitation rests on the principle of ‘one person, one vote, one value’, associated with uniformity of representation under Article 81(2).
accepted.tq: Discriminate among similar-looking formulations of the electoral equality principle.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Delimitation Commission is correct?
1. It is constituted under an Act of Parliament.
2. It works with the Election Commission of India.
3. Its orders may be modified by either House of Parliament.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Commission is constituted under parliamentary legislation and works with the ECI. Its orders cannot be modified by the Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assemblies, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘wrong authority’ trap to test who can modify delimitation orders.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the legal status of delimitation orders is correct?
o: They require approval by each State Assembly before becoming effective.
They cannot be challenged in a court and cannot be modified by the Lok Sabha or State Assemblies.
They can be challenged before any High Court as a matter of right.
They can be modified by the Lok Sabha through a simple resolution.
accepted.x: Delimitation Commission orders enjoy finality: they cannot be challenged in court or modified by the Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assemblies.
accepted.tq: Test the exceptional finality of a statutory Commission’s orders.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Delimitation Commissions in chronological order:
A. Commission chaired by Justice Kuldip Singh
B. Commission chaired by Justice J.L. Kapur constituted in 1963
C. Commission chaired by Justice N. Chandrasekhara Aiyar
D. Commission chaired by Justice J.L. Kapur constituted in 1973
accepted.x: The Commissions were constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002 respectively: N. Chandrasekhara Aiyar, J.L. Kapur, J.L. Kapur and Kuldip Singh.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence to the four constitution years rather than the repeated name of the chairperson.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Constitutional Amendment froze inter-State allocation of seats until 2000 on the basis of the 1971 Census?
accepted.x: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 froze inter-State seat allocation until 2000, using the 1971 Census as the basis.
accepted.tq: Link the amendment number with both its year and the census basis.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001:
1. It extended the freeze on inter-State seat allocation until after the first census following 2026.
2. It permitted rationalisation of constituencies on the basis of the 1991 Census.
3. It changed the total number of Lok Sabha seats on the basis of the 2001 Census.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 84th Amendment extended the freeze and allowed rationalisation using the 1991 Census. It did not change the total number of seats on the basis of the 2001 Census.
accepted.tq: Separate rationalisation of boundaries from alteration of the total number of seats.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal effect of the 87th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 was to:
o: Use the 2001 Census for redrawing boundaries without changing the total number of seats
End the freeze on inter-State seat allocation immediately
Restore the 1971 Census as the basis for delimitation and increase total seats
Abolish the Delimitation Commission and transfer its functions to Parliament
accepted.x: The 87th Amendment substituted the 2001 Census for boundary redrawing while keeping the total number of seats unchanged.
accepted.tq: Distinguish boundary redrawing from an increase in the total seat allocation.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Jammu and Kashmir Delimitation Commission — Justice Ranjana Desai
2. Assam delimitation — Election Commission of India
3. Assam delimitation became effective — August 2023
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Jammu and Kashmir Commission was headed by Justice Ranjana Desai, while Assam was delimited by the ECI with effect from August 2023.
accepted.tq: Combine the authority, chairperson and effective date to avoid state-wise confusion.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The orders of the Jammu and Kashmir Delimitation Commission headed by Justice Ranjana Desai became effective in:
accepted.x: The Jammu and Kashmir delimitation orders became effective in March and May 2022.
accepted.tq: Retain the paired effective months rather than only the year of the Commission’s work.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Tamil Nadu Assembly resolution is NOT correct?
o: It proposed freezing the Lok Sabha at 543 seats permanently.
It proposed retaining a 2.2:1 Lok Sabha to Rajya Sabha ratio.
It linked the proposed women’s quota to delimitation from 2029.
It proposed women’s quota from 2029 without linking it to delimitation.
accepted.x: The resolution proposed women’s reservation from 2029 without linking it to delimitation. It also proposed a permanent freeze at 543 Lok Sabha seats and retention of the 2.2:1 ratio.
accepted.tq: Locate the reversal of an expressly stated condition in a policy-resolution question.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The present number of elected Lok Sabha seats, as distinguished from the constitutional ceiling mentioned, is:
accepted.x: The Lok Sabha has 543 elected seats against a ceiling of 550, comprising 530 seats for States and 20 for Union Territories in the stated allocation framework.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the existing elected strength from the maximum ceiling.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The ceiling of 550 Lok Sabha seats mentioned in the constitutional framework consists of:
o: 500 seats for States and 50 seats for Union Territories
543 seats for States and 7 seats for Union Territories
520 seats for States and 30 seats for Union Territories
530 seats for States and 20 seats for Union Territories
accepted.x: The stated ceiling comprises 530 seats for the States and 20 seats for the Union Territories.
accepted.tq: Break a total into its State and Union Territory components.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Since which year have the per-State Lok Sabha seat numbers remained unchanged, as stated in the context of delimitation?
accepted.x: The per-State Lok Sabha seat numbers have remained unchanged since 1976.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of the constitutional freeze from the census years associated with it.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the former Anglo-Indian representation in the Lok Sabha is correct?
o: The two Anglo-Indian seats ended in 2020, making the older ceiling description outdated.
The Anglo-Indian seats were transferred to the Rajya Sabha in 2020.
The Anglo-Indian seats were increased from two to twenty in 2020.
The two Anglo-Indian seats continue to form part of the present elected strength.
accepted.x: The two Anglo-Indian nominated seats ended in 2020. Therefore, the older description of a maximum of 552 seats including two Anglo-Indians is stale.
accepted.tq: Identify the time-sensitive constitutional change behind an outdated numerical claim.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between Articles 81(2), 82 and 170 in delimitation?
o: Article 81(2) expresses uniformity of representation, while Articles 82 and 170 provide for constituency readjustment for Parliament and State Assemblies respectively.
Articles 82 and 170 prescribe the powers of the Election Commission but not constituency readjustment.
Article 81(2) deals only with Panchayat elections, while Articles 82 and 170 concern presidential elections.
Article 82 concerns Rajya Sabha elections and Article 170 concerns municipal elections.
accepted.x: Article 81(2) embodies uniformity of representation, while Articles 82 and 170 provide the constitutional basis for readjustment of Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies.
accepted.tq: Map each Article to its distinct constitutional function rather than its broad election subject.
accepted.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]
